A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MixCEM research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, intervention, distribution-shift, timing, and ablation experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds the MixIntCEM intervention-policy experiment in Appendix K and Figure 20.

M1.justification: V2 introduces MixIntCEM, combining MixCEM with IntCEM's training-time intervention sampling and learned intervention policy. This is a limited methodological extension; the original MixCEM architecture, entropy gating, loss, calibration, and inference procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same datasets and scenarios, including complete/incomplete classification tasks, TravelingBirds, visual corruptions, and MNIST-to-SVHN digit transfer. The new policy experiment reuses CUB and CUB-Incomplete under existing ID/OOD conditions.

E2.justification: Figure 20 newly evaluates IntCEM using its learned intervention policy as a comparator for MixIntCEM. V1's intervention comparisons used random selection. The existing baseline comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix K adds random-versus-learned policy evaluation, with hybrid hyperparameters inherited without a separate search. Appendix G also changes the stated default corruption level from 0.1% to 10%, matching Figure 4's existing caption. This corrects a reported setting but does not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new Appendix K investigates whether intervention-aware training preserves MixCEM's ID/OOD intervenability and whether learned selection improves on random interventions. The original corruption, domain-shift, spurious-correlation, bottleneck, and hyperparameter analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Table 1's three-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting and paired t-tests at p = 0.05, with the same significance convention in Table 6. V2 introduces no changed run-count disclosure or statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 20 adds MixIntCEM and learned-policy results: learned selection improves intervention curves, with the hybrid leading the displayed OOD comparisons, while learned-policy IntCEM sometimes leads on ID CUB. Existing numerical entries in Tables 1, 4, 5, and 6 and the original experimental plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B revises the existing likelihood argument: the approximation now combines contextual and prior-only predictions, deterministic encoders are explicit, and the final expression minimises a weighted loss instead of maximising losses. These are mathematical refinements and corrections; the CA and BI definitions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, three stated contributions, and concluding paragraph retain the same claims about leakage poisoning, the intervenability–incompleteness trade-off, and MixCEM's benefits for ID/OOD interventions. The policy extension does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 and Appendix K newly explain when pure IntCEM may remain preferable: concept-complete deployment restricted to ID inputs. V2 also qualifies the hybrid comparison by disclosing its lack of separate hyperparameter tuning. Existing MixCEM limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix K documents that MixIntCEM inherits the corresponding MixCEM and IntCEM hyperparameters without additional tuning. Existing hardware, software versions, and code/configuration access remain unchanged; the introduction's repository footnote repeats information already present in v1's resource appendix.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly positions IntCEM's intervention learning and MixCEM's embedding decomposition as complementary design principles that can be combined. The cited literature is otherwise retained; bibliography edits concern metadata rather than new works.

P1.justification: V2 expands explanations of CA/BI, rewrites parts of Appendix B, adds the policy discussion and Appendix K, and makes grammatical and terminology edits. The main narrative order is preserved, with acknowledgements and conference publication text added.

P2.justification: V2 adds the explanatory graphical models in Figure 6 and the policy comparison in Figure 20, relabels the existing MixCEM graphical model, and expands Table 1's caption. Existing experimental displays are retained with local repositioning and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The learned-policy experiment adds useful evidence and explicitly reports where IntCEM remains stronger, with the hybrid's tuning limitation disclosed. Correcting the default noise level and the derivation's loss direction improves consistency. These are incremental gains on top of the retained core evidence.
